Raise the ambition of the Barkpark Cloud site feature: Barkpark must be a COMPLETE STANDALONE solution — the box serves everything (content, site build+serve, its own TLS and DNS) with no external account required — AND be able to opt into Cloudflare or Vercel ON TOP to gain free superpowers: free wildcard TLS, DNS, unlimited-bandwidth global CDN, DDoS protection, tunnels (expose a private / no-public-IP box), and storage. blocks.text: Elevated north star (folds into charter vision)

content.value: Two laws, one shape. (1) STANDALONE-CORE: the box is a complete solution on its own — content + site build/serve + its own TLS + its own DNS, zero external accounts. With every provider disconnected, Barkpark still serves sites at a real URL. (2) PROVIDERS-ARE-PLUGINS: a connected cloud account is a capability plugin that only ADDS and degrades gracefully back to standalone — the exact Barkpark.Plugin law (all plugins off, it still works).

A connected provider exposes a CAPABILITY MENU: dns / tls / cdn / tunnel / storage / edge-fn / full-host. Cloudflare = free-superpower PRIMARY (free tier commercial-use-OK, unlimited bandwidth, Universal SSL wildcard, Tunnel, R2 zero-egress). Vercel = premium-DX option (Hobby is non-commercial, so it is the DX story, not the free-hosting story). The user gets global, DDoS-protected, custom-domain hosting for near-zero cost — the box stays the origin and the source of truth.

The single highest-leverage move: put Cloudflare in front of the Barkpark box — DNS + wildcard TLS at the edge + unlimited-bandwidth CDN + DDoS — with the box staying the ORIGIN. Highest capability-per-effort (mostly API calls + config, and it mirrors the existing Vercel adapter shape almost 1:1), AND it directly unblocks the epic's OWN wave-1 finish-line blockers: no wildcard cert, on_demand_tls never run on a live box, DNS-write unreachable from Elixir. Cloudflare terminates client TLS at the edge with a free wildcard (Universal SSL), so *.<instance>.barkpark.cloud subdomain-URL graduation no longer needs a live on_demand_tls run on the box.

blocks.title: Constraint: main CI is systemically RED; wave-1 is UNMERGED

content.value: Finished experience we are aiming at (Kinsta/Vercel bar): a user runs `bp cloud provider connect cloudflare` (paste a scoped API token, one time), then `bp cloud site expose my-blog --via cloudflare` — and within a minute the site is live on a custom domain, globally CDN'd, DDoS-protected, wildcard-TLS, with `bp cloud domain status` showing every rung green (DNS found → points to CF → CF proxying → origin healthy → serving). Disconnect the provider and the same site keeps serving from the box on its path-under-FQDN URL. The provider only ever ADDED reach; it never became load-bearing for correctness.

Tentative leanings (Decide finalizes after two explore rounds): (a) a CAPABILITY-PROVIDER CONTRACT — one behaviour family where each provider declares `capabilities/0 :: [:dns | :tls | :cdn | :tunnel | :storage | :edge_fn | :full_host]` and implements only the capability behaviours it supports; standalone = the null provider; connect = union of capabilities; disconnect = fall back to the box. (b) Mirror the Vercel adapter EXACTLY: a `BarkparkCloud.Cloudflare` context + `Cloudflare.Client` SEAM behaviour + `Cloudflare.Real` (:httpc verified-TLS) + `Cloudflare.Fake` (in-memory €0 double), config-at-call-time client resolution, `configured?/0` fail-closed, per-instance API token encrypted in Registry.Vault. (c) Full-Strict composition: CF orange-cloud proxies to the box; the box installs a free CF Origin CA cert in Caddy (long-lived, no on_demand_tls) so client→CF and CF→origin are both TLS. (d) The DNS write that is Go-only today (internal/hetzner/dns.go over hcloud) gets an Elixir-reachable sibling via the CF API — the control plane writes DNS directly.

Deliverables THIS wave: (1) fold the standalone-core + capability-provider north star into the charter Vision + a new decision block. (2) a validated capability-provider CONTRACT (the menu abstraction) + the Cloudflare-in-front (DNS+TLS+CDN) design, pressure-tested against wave-1's real files. (3) file + PERFECT bp tasks for the Cloudflare-in-front build (actual build lands a LATER wave once CI greens + wave-1 merges). (4) at most 1-3 SMALL dependency-light + additive build slices ONLY if genuinely independent — candidates: a `Cloudflare.Client` behaviour + `Cloudflare.Fake` scaffold (new files, mirrors vercel/client.ex + fake.ex), or a capability-provider contract module. Everything else = backlog.

blocks.text: Elevated north star (folds into charter vision)

content.value: Two laws, one shape. (1) STANDALONE-CORE: the box is a complete solution on its own — content + site build/serve + its own TLS + its own DNS, zero external accounts. With every provider disconnected, Barkpark still serves sites at a real URL. (2) PROVIDERS-ARE-PLUGINS: a connected cloud account is a capability plugin that only ADDS and degrades gracefully back to standalone — the exact Barkpark.Plugin law (all plugins off, it still works).

A connected provider exposes a CAPABILITY MENU: dns / tls / cdn / tunnel / storage / edge-fn / full-host. Cloudflare = free-superpower PRIMARY (free tier commercial-use-OK, unlimited bandwidth, Universal SSL wildcard, Tunnel, R2 zero-egress). Vercel = premium-DX option (Hobby is non-commercial, so it is the DX story, not the free-hosting story). The user gets global, DDoS-protected, custom-domain hosting for near-zero cost — the box stays the origin and the source of truth.

The single highest-leverage move: put Cloudflare in front of the Barkpark box — DNS + wildcard TLS at the edge + unlimited-bandwidth CDN + DDoS — with the box staying the ORIGIN. Highest capability-per-effort (mostly API calls + config, and it mirrors the existing Vercel adapter shape almost 1:1), AND it directly unblocks the epic's OWN wave-1 finish-line blockers: no wildcard cert, on_demand_tls never run on a live box, DNS-write unreachable from Elixir. Cloudflare terminates client TLS at the edge with a free wildcard (Universal SSL), so *.<instance>.barkpark.cloud subdomain-URL graduation no longer needs a live on_demand_tls run on the box.

Real separates PURE request builders from @impl fns that chain through a private request/1; token/0 and request/1 FAIL CLOSED (:not_configured / :http_client_not_configured) and never touch the wire unconfigured; reuses Billing.HttpClient (no new transport). Fake is a deterministic €0 double (sha256-truncated ids, Process-dict recording, fail- sentinels). VERDICT: faithful, correct, honest. The reviewer added a Real.request/1 decode-path describe block (stub http_client injected via config — the GitHub.Real real_test precedent) to close the one vacuous-green gap: the builder tested only pure builders + fail-closed guards, leaving the module's only non-trivial runtime logic (2xx→decode→extract, non-2xx→typed {:cloudflare_http_error}, transport-error passthrough, unexpected-shape) unproven. Adds "cloudflare" to Registry.Provider.@kinds and a validate_credential_shape/3 clause that accepts EITHER a bare API token OR a {api_token, account_id?, zone_id?} JSON blob, rejecting blank / JSON-missing-token / blank-api_token; rides the existing encrypted_token column with NO migration (D14). Adversarial edge check: numeric/array JSON is treated as a bare token (decode is non-object → not a blob), which is harmless and intentional per D14 (a non-blank string suffices for the bare-token path; real CF tokens never parse as JSON). Error attaches to the virtual :credential, never the ciphertext column. Gate 18/18.
